# SPECIAL INSTRUCTIONS FOR THE `/development` BRANCH ## Installation ### Python server 0. Install `uv` - https://github.com/astral-sh/uv?tab=readme-ov-file#installation 1. clone the repo - `git clone https://github.com/freemocap/freemocap` 2. Change directory to the repo: - `cd freemocap` 3. **Change to the `development` branch:** - `git switch development` 4. Create virtual environment: - `uv venv` 5. Activate virtual environment - Windows: `.venv/bin/activate` - Mac/Linux: `source .venv/bin/activate` 6. Install dependencies - `uv sync` — installs skellytracker with NVIDIA GPU acceleration on Windows/Linux, or CPU-only on macOS, automatically - No supported GPU on Windows/Linux? Force the CPU-only build instead: `uv sync --no-default-groups --group cpu` ### React GUI 0. Install Node.js - https://nodejs.org/en/download/ 1. Change directory to the `freemocap-ui` folder - `cd freemocap-ui` 2. Install dependencies - `npm install` ## Run the FreeMoCap application in development mode 1. Start the Python Server: - `python freemocap/__main__.py` - The server should start on `http://localhost:8005` 2. Start the React GUI: - `npm run dev` - An Electron window should pop up with the FreeMoCap GUI ## Build the FreeMoCap application (NOTE - This is not necessary for development, and does not handle the Python server yet) 1. Change directory to the `freemocap/freemocap-ui` folder - `npm run build` - The build will be in the `freemocap/freemocap-ui/releases` folder --- --- # STANDARD README CONTINUES BELOW ___ ___ ___

The FreeMoCap Project

A free-and-open-source, hardware-and-software-agnostic, minimal-cost, research-grade, motion capture system and platform for decentralized scientific research, education, and training

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/15314521/192062522-2a8d9305-f181-4869-a4b9-1aa068e094c9.mp4 -- ## QUICKSTART #### 0. Create a a Python 3.9 through 3.11 environment (python3.11 recommended)¶ #### 1. Install software via [pip](https://pypi.org/project/freemocap/#description): `freemocap` requires the `cuda` or `cpu` extra to be specified — plain `pip install freemocap` will install without its tracker. Pick one: ``` pip install freemocap[cuda] # Windows/Linux with an NVIDIA GPU ``` ``` pip install freemocap[cpu] # macOS, or Windows/Linux without a supported GPU ``` #### 2. Launch the GUI by entering the command: ``` freemocap ``` #### 3. A GUI should pop up that looks like this: #### 4. Have fun! It might break! Work in Progress lol #### 5. [Join the Discord and let us know how it went!](https://discord.gg/nxv5dNTfKT) ___ ## Install/run from source code (i.e. the code in this repo) This repo's dependencies (`skellytracker`, `skellycam`, etc.) are pulled from private git repos via [`uv`](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv), so `conda` + `pip install -e .` will not work here — use `uv` instead: 1) Install `uv` - https://github.com/astral-sh/uv?tab=readme-ov-file#installation 2) Clone the repository ```bash git clone https://github.com/freemocap/freemocap ``` 3) Navigate into the newly cloned/downloaded `freemocap` folder ```bash cd freemocap ``` 4) Create a virtual environment ```bash uv venv ``` 5) Install dependencies ```bash uv sync ``` This installs `skellytracker` with NVIDIA GPU acceleration on Windows/Linux, or CPU-only on macOS, automatically. If you're on Windows/Linux without a supported GPU, force the CPU-only build instead: ```bash uv sync --no-default-groups --group cpu ``` 6) Launch the Python server ```bash uv run python freemocap/__main__.py ``` The server starts on `http://localhost:8005`. 7) In a separate terminal, launch the React/Electron GUI (requires [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/download/)): ```bash cd freemocap-ui npm install npm run dev ``` An Electron window should pop up with the FreeMoCap GUI! ___ ## Documentation Our documenation is hosted at: https://freemocap.github.io/documentation/index_md.html That site is built using `writerside` from this repository: https://github.com/freemocap/documentation ___ ### Contribution Guidelines Please read our contribution doc: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## Related [//]: # (* [project-name](#) - Project description) ## Maintainers * [Jon Matthis](https://github.com/jonmatthis) * [Endurance Idehen](https://github.com/endurance) ## License This project is licensed under the APGL License - see the [LICENSE](LICENSE) file for details. SPECIAL INSTRUCTIONS FOR THE /development BRANCH

Installation

Python server

  1. Install uv
    • https://github.com/astral-sh/uv?tab=readme-ov-file#installation
  2. clone the repo
    • git clone https://github.com/freemocap/freemocap
  3. Change directory to the repo:
    • cd freemocap
  4. Change to the development branch:
    • git switch development
  5. Create virtual environment:
    • uv venv
  6. Activate virtual environment
    • Windows: .venv/bin/activate
    • Mac/Linux: source .venv/bin/activate
  7. Install dependencies
  • uv sync — installs skellytracker with NVIDIA GPU acceleration on Windows/Linux, or CPU-only on macOS, automatically
  • No supported GPU on Windows/Linux? Force the CPU-only build instead: uv sync --no-default-groups --group cpu

React GUI

  1. Install Node.js
    • https://nodejs.org/en/download/
  2. Change directory to the freemocap-ui folder
    • cd freemocap-ui
  3. Install dependencies
    • npm install

Run the FreeMoCap application in development mode

  1. Start the Python Server:
    • python freemocap/__main__.py
    • The server should start on http://localhost:8005
  2. Start the React GUI:
    • npm run dev
    • An Electron window should pop up with the FreeMoCap GUI

Build the FreeMoCap application

(NOTE - This is not necessary for development, and does not handle the Python server yet)

  1. Change directory to the freemocap/freemocap-ui folder
    • npm run build
    • The build will be in the freemocap/freemocap-ui/releases folder

STANDARD README CONTINUES BELOW

The FreeMoCap Project

A free-and-open-source, hardware-and-software-agnostic, minimal-cost, research-grade, motion capture system and platform for decentralized scientific research, education, and training

2022-03-09_FreeMoCap_Clips_SHORT_compressed.mp4

--

QUICKSTART

0. Create a a Python 3.9 through 3.11 environment (python3.11 recommended)¶

1. Install software via pip:

freemocap requires the cuda or cpu extra to be specified — plain pip install freemocap will install without its tracker. Pick one:

pip install freemocap[cuda]   # Windows/Linux with an NVIDIA GPU

pip install freemocap[cpu]    # macOS, or Windows/Linux without a supported GPU

2. Launch the GUI by entering the command:

freemocap

3. A GUI should pop up that looks like this:

4. Have fun! It might break! Work in Progress lol

5. Join the Discord and let us know how it went!

Install/run from source code (i.e. the code in this repo)

This repo's dependencies (skellytracker, skellycam, etc.) are pulled from private git repos via uv, so conda + pip install -e . will not work here — use uv instead:

  1. Install uv

    • https://github.com/astral-sh/uv?tab=readme-ov-file#installation

  2. Clone the repository

git clone https://github.com/freemocap/freemocap
  1. Navigate into the newly cloned/downloaded freemocap folder
cd freemocap
  1. Create a virtual environment
uv venv
  1. Install dependencies
uv sync

This installs skellytracker with NVIDIA GPU acceleration on Windows/Linux, or CPU-only on macOS, automatically. If you're on Windows/Linux without a supported GPU, force the CPU-only build instead:

uv sync --no-default-groups --group cpu
  1. Launch the Python server
uv run python freemocap/__main__.py

The server starts on http://localhost:8005.

  1. In a separate terminal, launch the React/Electron GUI (requires Node.js):
cd freemocap-ui
npm install
npm run dev

An Electron window should pop up with the FreeMoCap GUI!

Documentation

Our documenation is hosted at: https://freemocap.github.io/documentation/index_md.html

That site is built using writerside from this repository: https://github.com/freemocap/documentation

Contribution Guidelines

Please read our contribution doc: CONTRIBUTING.md

releases.body:
FreeMoCap  v2.0.0-alpha.23 comes with some nice updates to our video importing and Blender functionality courtesy of @philipqueen , @ajc27-git  and @slrove 

-  [SkellySync]((https://github.com/freemocap/skellysync)) has been updated for v2.0 functionality, meaning you can now synchronize videos upon import using either audio or brightness-dependent syncing!
- We should now be fully Blender 5 compatible
- Foot-locking methods in the freemocap-blender-addon have been updated
- Exported Blender scenes should, for videos recorded using the FreeMoCap software, now match the camera framerate instead of defaulting to 24fps. Videos synchronized or imported from outside of FreeMoCap will still use that default framerate.

* Blender updates and skellysync by @aaroncherian in https://github.com/freemocap/freemocap/pull/879
* Route Windows CUDA to cloudflare by @aaroncherian in https://github.com/freemocap/freemocap/pull/880


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/freemocap/freemocap/compare/v2.0.0-alpha.18...v2.0.0-alpha.23

releases.name: v2.0.0-alpha.21
releases.body:
FreeMoCap v2.0.0-alpha.21 comes with lots of bug fixes, courtesy of @philipqueen and @slrove.

- You can now import synchronized videos into the software. The ability to synchronize pre-recorded videos (as is present in 1.0) will be coming soon! 
- The calculated FPS from recorded videos is now used as the input to the Butterworth filter. *However* if you are using pre-recorded, imported videos, you will still want to set this yourself. 
- The bug regarding single camera recordings needing a calibration to process has been fixed. 
- The UI is now more explicit about currently only MediaPipe-based recordings being able to be exported into Blender. (We do plan to make this functionality available to RTMPose-based recordings in the future though)
- And a host of other under-the-hood bug fixes. 

## What's Changed
* Skeleton refitting and UI updates by @aaroncherian in https://github.com/freemocap/freemocap/pull/843
* Bump version v2.0.0-alpha.18 -> v2.0.0-alpha.19 by @aaroncherian in https://github.com/freemocap/freemocap/pull/844
* Fix hand file naming bug by @aaroncherian in https://github.com/freemocap/freemocap/pull/846
* Bump version v2.0.0-alpha.19 -> v2.0.0-alpha.20

aiSummary.oneLiner: A free, open-source motion capture platform designed for hardware-agnostic research, biomechanics analysis, and indie animation workflows.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: FreeMoCap provides a minimal-cost, research-grade motion capture system that is completely hardware and software agnostic. It processes standard video input using skellytracker and NVIDIA GPU acceleration to extract precise skeletal movement data. The system offers a Python backend server coupled with a React/Electron GUI to deliver a full-stack solution for capturing and visualizing motion. By removing the need for expensive, proprietary setups, it democratizes access to motion capture technology for scientific research, remote physical therapy, and indie game development. This allows motion capture data collection using standard smartphones or webcams without dedicated studio spaces.
keyFeatures: Hardware agnostic tracking: Functions entirely without requiring specialized infrared cameras or proprietary motion capture hardware setups.
NVIDIA GPU acceleration: Leverages local hardware on Windows and Linux to provide high-performance, real-time skeletal tracking.
React graphical interface: Includes a polished, interactive desktop application built with Electron for intuitive user control.
Research-grade precision: Delivers accurate skeletal tracking suitable for strict scientific analysis and detailed animation tasks.
Decentralized data collection: Enables remote and widespread biomechanics data gathering by removing the need for dedicated studio spaces.

useCases.title: Scientific biomechanics research
useCases.description: Researchers capture accurate human movement data for kinematic analysis without needing access to a million-dollar lab facility.

useCases.title: Indie game animation
useCases.description: Small development teams create realistic 3D character animations for games using standard smartphone video recordings.

useCases.title: Remote physical therapy
useCases.description: Clinicians analyze patient movement remotely by processing standard video recordings of prescribed rehabilitation exercises.

useCases.title: Educational demonstration
useCases.description: Teachers visually demonstrate biomechanical principles and kinematics to students using an accessible, interactive desktop application.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Biomechanics researchers, indie game developers, physical therapists, and educators who need accessible, high-quality motion capture capabilities.
